correctness.rationale: The vertex-case partition gives exact D, with double-counted singleton/singleton intersections subtracted and single-side whole sets added. Symbolic degree-three minor proves negative log-concavity for all n>=13, and the exact finite coefficient formula yields a complete 11-order positive certificate. A standard log-concavity-preserving convolution proves total domination LC; known monotonic probability coupling and an exact middle/tail count prove strict unimodality for all n>=4. Standalone direct subset enumeration for n=2..7 and finite all-coefficient checks corroborate but are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact sharp family-wide LC phase transition at n=13 in ordinary domination, despite strict unimodality on positive support, on connected regular vertex-transitive bipartite graphs. It reveals a clean separation from total-domination coefficient behavior on identical graphs. The structural enumerator explains the phenomenon and attaches a mathematically motivated finite cutoff to an active research topic in graph-polynomial coefficient shapes; it is not a random finite invariant or title-only variant.
